bibliographic.title: A Privacy by Design Framework for Large Language Model-Based Applications for Children
bibliographic.authors: Diana Addae; Diana Rogachova; Nafiseh Kahani; Masoud Barati; Michael Christensen; Chen Zhou
bibliographic.citation_apa: Addae, D., Rogachova, D., Kahani, N., Barati, M., Christensen, M., & Zhou, C. (2026). A privacy by design framework for large language model-based applications for children. [Venue unclear].

methodology.study_design: conceptual framework with literature-based operational control mapping and illustrative case study
methodology.technology_context: Large Language Model-based applications for children, including educational tools, conversational agents, and LLM-powered storytelling bots

eligibility.decision_rationale: The article proposes a Privacy-by-Design framework mapping GDPR, PIPEDA, COPPA, UNCRC, and AADC principles to LLM application stages, including operational monitoring and ongoing validation, with a case study of an LLM-based educational tutor for children under 13. It is relevant to governance, privacy, compliance, and regulated educational LLM use, but the primary contribution is children's data privacy rather than conversational governance mechanisms such as oversight, contestation, or accountability in dialogue systems.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Extracted bibliographic metadata is corrupted; only front matter and a fragment of page 5 were provided, so peer-review status, venue, methods detail, results, and limitations cannot be fully verified.

appraisal.notes: Appraisal is limited to the abstract, introduction, and one partial sentence from a later section. The stated approach—mapping regulatory principles to LLM lifecycle stages and illustrating application via a case study—fits a methodological framework paper, but sampling, literature search methods, analysis procedures, results, and limitations are not described in the provided text.

cerqual.explanation: The framework objective and lifecycle mapping are clearly articulated and internally coherent in the available text. Relevance to regulated LLM governance is moderate-to-high for privacy and operational controls, but confidence is moderated because only partial text is available and empirical validation beyond a case study is unclear.

coding.theme: Privacy and data governance framework for LLM-based applications targeting children
coding.subtheme: Regulatory alignment across data collection, training, monitoring, and validation in educational/conversational LLM contexts

governance of conversational/educational LLM applications for vulnerable users

synthesis.main_claim: A Privacy-by-Design framework can guide proactive, risk-averse design of LLM-based applications for children by mapping privacy regulatory principles to LLM lifecycle stages and supporting compliance through technical and organizational controls.
synthesis.contribution: Integrates multiple privacy regulations and child-rights design standards into a staged framework for LLM applications, discusses operational controls from recent literature, and demonstrates application through an LLM-based educational tutor case study for children under 13.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as supporting evidence on privacy governance, regulatory compliance, and operational monitoring/validation controls for LLM applications in regulated children's and educational contexts; secondary support for conversational LLM applications where privacy and lifecycle governance are relevant.
